sources.entry: panda3d - 3D game engine developed jointly by Disney and contributors from around the world.

summary.one_liner: Panda3D is an open-source 3D game engine and rendering framework usable from Python and C++ programs.
summary.what_it_does: Panda3D is a framework for 3D rendering and game development for Python and C++ programs. The README describes it as free for any purpose, including commercial use, under the Modified BSD License. It is installable from PyPI with pip, with a development build available via a pre-release pip command. The repository includes a makepanda build script that compiles the engine from source on Windows, Linux, macOS, FreeBSD, and for Android cross-compilation to wheels, with options for optional features and packaging (installers, .deb/.rpm, .whl). Tests run with PyTest. The README points to a gallery, feature list, documentation, and community forums and IRC for help.
use_cases: package a Python app for Android with build_apps
compile a custom game engine from source
commercial game development with a permissive license
notable: Usable from both Python and C++ programs
Modified BSD License, free for commercial use
Installable with a single pip command
Build script supports Windows, Linux, macOS, FreeBSD, and Android cross-compilation to wheels
Works with build_apps to produce .apk or .aab bundles
caveats: Building from source requires many third-party dependency libraries and development packages
Enabling Eigen on Windows can make the build take hours
Android builds require the Android SDK/NDK and a matching Python 3.13 host
